clue.text: "Domesticate smooth snake, doubly smooth", written in (way back) by 6down 14down

parts.note: to domesticate an animal is to train it
to sand wood is to smooth it
the boa is a constricting snake
two more carpentry verbs for smoothing, the sandpaper one again and the one done with a bladed tool, joined by a loose T

explanation.surface: A title in quotation marks, as if someone were taming and polishing a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase splits the song title in unexpected places, with the second smoothing word used twice. The T has no clue word of its own, so read this as a punning rendering rather than strict wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Burt Bacharach wrote the music of this 1964 hit, so it is a song he composed long ago.

clue.text: 252 gallons of wine is capital!

parts.note: a tun is a large cask, an old measure of 252 gallons of wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a huge quantity of wine is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like old-fashioned praise; it is the definition, a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia in North Africa.

clue.text: See 1 across
One trim turning up with smart clothing — an Italian

indicators.note: the smart word wraps around the reversed piece like clothes around a body

parts.note: neat means smart and tidy

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the words are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Roman numeral one
to lop is to trim or cut back
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sprucing up a smartly dressed Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' is the container signal: the smart word is worn around the reversed pair, and the final article is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan comes from Naples, so the person is an Italian by birth.

clue.text: The wife's providing support for line on high profile Tory family

parts.note: an arc is a curved line; 'on' puts it on top in a down entry
the wife's thing is hers, and it sits underneath, supporting what comes above

explanation.surface: Gossip about a wife propping up her prominent Conservative husband's family.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'support for' puts HERS below ARC. Jeffrey Archer, novelist and Conservative peer, and his wife Mary are the family meant; The Archers is also a long-running BBC radio soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeffrey and Mary Archer are a well-known Conservative couple whose surname, pluralised, names the family.

clue.text: Having organised a cover-up, does a stretch

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the words are written from the bottom to the top

parts.note: set as in arranged or set up
taken as written
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: Someone who organised a cover-up ends up serving time in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does a stretch' looks like a prison sentence; it means widens. 'Cover-up' reads as a scandal, but splits into cover plus the direction indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate is to widen or expand, which is what something stretching does.

clue.text: See 1 across
Composer's composer about to 'arm himself with sawn-off arm

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a musician admired by other musicians

definitions.text: about to 'arm himself with sawn-off arm
definitions.meaning: setter's reading: a cockney-flavoured hint, the dropped H of 'arm pointing at the composer's first name, with BACH, another composer, inside the surname

explanation.surface: A musicians' musician about to injure himself with a shortened weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname contains BACH, so this composer holds a composer. The rest of the wordplay is too loose to map letter for letter, so read it as a playful hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Burt Bacharach was an American songwriter famous for hits written with lyricist Hal David.

clue.text: A biography with heart sent back by 6 14

indicators.note: heart is the middle of the word, and sent back turns those middle letters round

parts.note: a life is a biography

explanation.surface: A life story with its core reversed, written by somebody named elsewhere in the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with heart sent back' swaps the middle letters IF of LIFE round to FI.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the famous title associated with the name spelt across lights 6 and 14.

clue.text: It's wise to safeguard misuse of relic, as this would be …

indicators.note: to safeguard something is to keep it protected inside

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that mistreating a holy relic would be wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis invites you to finish the sentence: misusing a relic would be ... the answer, and 'It's' stands for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating a sacred object with disrespect is the textbook example of a profane violation.

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dingy hotel suite giving a sleazy impression.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is a dark outline picture of a shape against a light background.

clue.text: Still one remains elusive?

parts.note: yet as in still, so far
Roman numeral one

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer while the first two words build it.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas has famously never been captured or proven to exist.

clue.text: Six-footer Paul's significant? That's hypothetical stuff

parts.note: an insect has six feet
Paul is the setter, so Paul is 'I'

explanation.surface: A tall man named Paul being important, then a nod to theoretical physics.
explanation.walkthrough: Six-footer is a crossword favourite for an insect, not a tall person; Paul's = Paul is, and the setter calls himself I.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimatter, made of antiparticles, was long a theoretical substance of physics and science fiction.

clue.text: Members of a gang and fragmented, you might say

indicators.note: this signals a playful reading of fragmented as 'in bits', placing one word inside the other

parts.note: something fragmented is in bits
taken as written

explanation.surface: Members of a gang that has broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: Fragmented means 'in bits', and that little 'in' is what puts the conjunction inside the fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandits are outlaws who rob in armed groups, so each is one of a gang.

clue.text: Warrior setting island on fire

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like flames; it means dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks were horsemen of the Russian and Ukrainian steppes renowned as fighters.

Component of a machine seen as an intricate kind of puzzle

clue.text: Second notion back to front

parts.note: an idea is a notion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal; it is a noun, an assistant, as in a duelling second.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is a helper or deputy, which is exactly what an aide is.

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East
taken as written
